table_notes.text: All monetary figures are in the named reporting currency, millions, at the source’s precision. Each row is a different fiscal year-end, not a common calendar-year/TTM comparison. R&D is total company expense, not disclosed AI-only spending. Blank/null means not separately disclosed or not verified, never zero.

Label the columns “Capex (scope note)” and “CFO − shown capex”. Simple FCF is an analyst bridge, not a standardized GAAP measure or cash necessarily available for distribution. Scope varies by issuer; stock compensation, financing principal, leases, acquisitions, intangibles and growth investment can materially change economic cash returns.

AMZN gross profit subtracts cost of sales but leaves fulfillment and technology/infrastructure in operating expenses. ORCL gross profit is derived from directly reported cloud/software, hardware and services costs before separately presented intangible amortization. Neither is a fully like-for-like gross margin with all other firms.

IBM uses net capex US$1,617m, not verified gross PP&E payments. Shown CFO−net capex is US$11,576m. Issuer FCF US$14,734m also removes financing-receivable cash movements; issuer rounding causes a US$1m bridge difference. Preserve reported GP US$39,297m even if rounded revenue−cost differs by US$1m.

NVDA, LRCX and ANET capex includes intangibles; DELL and HPE includes capitalized software. Do not label these five rows as pure physical PP&E. NVIDIA’s company FCF also deducts US$101m principal payments, so it is US$96,575m versus the shown bridge US$96,676m.

MSFT and META shown FCF excludes finance-lease principal; META company FCF is US$43,585m after US$2,524m principal versus shown US$46,109m. INTC shown capex US$14,646m excludes another US$3,026m of PP&E classified in financing cash flows. These are not total infrastructure cash-cost measures.

AMZN shown capex is gross cash PP&E US$131,819m; issuer FCF US$11,194m deducts net capex US$128,320m after US$3,499m proceeds/incentives, versus shown bridge US$7,695m. MU shown capex is gross PP&E before government incentives; its reported adjusted FCF uses different treatment. Do not substitute the larger issuer measures in a same-label column.

Shown capex omits separately disclosed intangible/software investment: ARM US$30m purchases plus US$67m obligation payments; ASML EUR57.6m; MRVL US$4.5m licenses; Tokyo Electron JPY10,457m; MediaTek TWD10,360.5m; TSMC intangible purchases separately reported; Samsung KRW4,630,970m; SK hynix KRW1,060,419m; Lenovo US$596.979m; Vertiv US$6.4m. Do not claim a fully harmonized economic FCF ranking.

EQIX shown capex US$4,311m excludes US$994m real-estate acquisitions. CFO−shown capex is −US$400m; company FCF is −US$2,572m under a broader definition. Show FY2025 AFFO US$3,761m / US$38.33 per diluted share nearby, while explaining that AFFO does not deduct every growth investment. Use development funding and AFFO, not ordinary tech P/E alone.

AMD CFO US$6,493m and capex US$974m both use continuing operations; net income US$4,335m includes US$66m discontinued income. Foxconn capex is the earnings-presentation capital-expenditure measure; do not silently relabel it independently verified gross cash PP&E.

Net income is not uniform across owners: PLTR is common-shareholder income; SNOW, INTC, MediaTek, TSMC, Tokyo Electron and Foxconn are parent/owner-attributable. INTC −US$267m parent income differs from +US$26m consolidated. HPE US$57m is attributable to HPE but common-shareholder income is −US$59m after preferred dividends. ORCL US$17,087m is consolidated versus common US$16,984m; SMCI is before preferred dividends. Add a simple P/C/Common scope marker or explicit footnote.

Lenovo, Samsung, SK hynix and EQIX figures are consolidated, including noncontrolling interests, rather than solely income available to listed ordinary shareholders. Do not change the numerators without changing the stated scope.

TSMC uses Taiwan-IFRS figures here; do not splice SEC-IFRS net margin into this row. ASML uses US GAAP here; US-GAAP CFO EUR12,658.5m differs from IFRS CFO EUR13,826.5m. Preserve the selected basis across each row.

Net profit is reported, not normalized: Alphabet/Amazon include investment valuation gains; Microsoft FY2026 includes US$5.0bn OpenAI investment impacts; Meta FY2025 includes US$15.93bn tax charge; Broadcom FY2025 includes US$2.1bn tax benefit; Qualcomm FY2026 includes US$5.7bn valuation-allowance release; Marvell includes US$1,830.4m pretax business-sale gain; IBM includes tax-resolution benefits. Do not read headline net margins as recurring operating returns.

SBC is added back in CFO and remains an ownership cost. SNOW FY2026 SBC US$1,599.547m and TEAM US$1,606.561m exceed their shown simple FCF. PLTR and NOW issuer adjusted FCF also add back specified cash items; retain the simple bridge in the common column.

AMZN does not separately disclose R&D; technology/infrastructure US$108,521m is broader and must not fill the R&D blank. EQIX R&D is not separately disclosed. VRT US$441.7m is engineering plus R&D (ER&D). SK hynix expensed R&D KRW6,465,637m differs from gross spending KRW6,732,527m because KRW266,890m was capitalized.

MediaTek capex is reported only to TWD0.1m although other inputs are to TWD0.001m; the many decimal places in derived FCF do not improve capex precision. Tokyo Electron issuer figures are rounded down to JPY1m. Foxconn combines TWD1m presentation data with separately retrieved finer R&D precision. IBM table rounding is a source characteristic, not an arithmetic error.

Oracle FY2026 CFO includes US$4,592m customer prepayments with a significant financing component. Current cash inflow therefore also represents future delivery obligations; do not treat it all as mature recurring cash earnings.
Apple’s low cash PP&E reflects its ownership footprint. Outsourced manufacturing and external infrastructure still have costs; low owned capex does not mean the whole supply chain is capital-light.
